summary.brief: A man braids four white strands into a round braid and finishes by tying an overhand knot.
summary.detailed: In a dimly lit indoor setting with a dark wooden or reddish background, a man’s hands manipulate four white strands. He holds the strands between the thumb and middle finger of his left hand, forming a small loop, while his right hand pulls each strand over the others, passes it behind and over the remaining strands, and then draws it through the loop before tightening. This crossing‑and‑pulling sequence is repeated for each strand multiple times, building up a cylindrical, round braid. After the braid is formed, he adjusts the tension, attempts a few simple and double knots to secure the ends, loosens and retightens them, and finally ties a clear overhand knot to finish the braid.

action.detailed: Hold the four strands between the thumb and middle finger of your left hand, use your right hand to cross each strand over the others, pull each crossed strand through the loop formed by your left hand’s fingers, tighten, repeat the steps until a cylindrical braid forms, then secure the ends with an overhand knot.

summary.brief: A man braids four white strands into a round sling and finishes it with securing knots.
summary.detailed: The close‑up video shows a man’s hands against a dim, wooden background illuminated by a warm orange‑red light. He begins by spreading four white strands and pinching them between the thumb, index and middle fingers of his left hand. Using his right hand, he pulls one strand over the others, threads it through the loop formed between the left middle and index fingers, and slides the loop down to tighten. He repeats this crossing‑through‑loop motion for each strand, building up a smooth cylindrical braid as the process is performed twice for each of the four strands. After the braid has sufficient length, he creates a four‑part bridge by passing strands behind and over each other as described in the spoken instructions, continuously tightening the structure. Finally, he secures the braid by tying a series of half‑hitch (and double half‑hitch) knots, pulling the ends tight until the completed round‑braid sling is held firmly in his hands.

action.detailed: Hold the four strands between the thumb and fingers of the left hand, use the right hand to pull each strand over the others and thread it through the loop formed between the left middle and index fingers, slide the loop down to tighten, repeat for all strands to build the round braid, then form the bridge by passing strands behind and over each other and finish by securing the braid with half‑hitch knots.
